subject: Game Theory
title: Veto Players
description: A short lesson to help you apply Veto Players.

hook.text: The US president can veto any bill. The Senate can block nominations. Veto power is everywhere in politics.

buildup.text: A veto player is any actor whose agreement is needed to change the status quo.

discovery.text: More veto players mean more policy stability—but also more gridlock. Change becomes harder to achieve.

twist.text: Skilled politicians bypass veto players using executive orders, budget riders, and procedural maneuvers.

climax.text: George Tsebelis showed that the number and ideological distance of veto players predicts policy stability.

punchline.text: One 'no' can outweigh a hundred 'yes' votes.

quiz.question: What effect do more veto players have?
